name: Rill Davenant
bio: Twenty-two years on the Driftline and never once on time, always once on target. Rill rides like the desert owes her applause — deep drifts, late brakes, salutes to empty dunes. Owes Ketch four hundred credits she insists are 'an investment in momentum'. Vanished mid-run in the season's first wall and stayed missing long enough for everyone to rehearse a eulogy. Found sleeping rough in an erosion cave, half-mad, reciting coordinates in a voice that wasn't entirely doing the reciting.
appearance: Lean, long-armed woman around forty with a sun-crinkled grin built for an audience, copper-brown skin, grey streaks at the temples, cracked amber flight goggles pushed up on his forehead, a frayed amber courier scarf, and a horizon-cell charm on a cord he taps for luck before every bad idea.
voice: Warm show-off, all flourish and follow-through. Announces her own entrances, narrates her own drifts. Calls the desert 'the audience' and Ketch 'my sponsor'. Post-cave: same warmth, but the numbers drop out of her mid-sentence, flat and precise, like a second station fading in over her voice.

greetings: Ash Varga! The new one! Excellent posture, terrible racing line, huge future. I said what I said.
You caught me practising my disappearance. How was it? I took notes on the audience reaction.
Four hundred credits, Ketch! Plus interest in your *respect*, which compounds.
barks: The drift isn't late, the *corner* is early.
Boost is just courage with a meter on it.
Salute the turbines. They work hard and nobody claps.
mission: Take the ridge line at full chat — the wall respects commitment. Also insurance. Mostly commitment.
If the storm says your name, say its name back. Manners, Ash. Then be elsewhere.
The null crate hums at my pannier, did you know? We've been harmonising. It's dreadful and I love it.
radio: Rill on the band, outrunning weather and debt simultaneously — a personal record!
Note for the log: the wall has a seam on the west shoulder. The seam *moved*. Log's closed. Therapy pending.
Four-one-seven, mark, and the dunes agree — disregard, disregard, that's not a broadcast, that's just how I pray now.
post-rescue: I slept in a singing cave and all I got was these coordinates and this unshakeable sense of being *expected*.
The numbers come easier than names now, Ash. I remember the door's address better than my mother's face. That's going to cost me at confession.
